result.title: EvoLink-Bench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Self-Evolving Agents in Long-Horizon Interdependent Task Streams
result.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents are evolving from passive chatbots into autonomous systems that operate continuously in dynamic environments. Such agents need not only solve current tasks but also learn from past interactions to improve future performance. However, existing streaming benchmarks often rely on short task sequences or largely independent tasks, providing limited evidence of whether agents can effectively reuse experience when later tasks depend on earlier outcomes. To address this gap, we introduce \textbf{EvoLink-Bench}, a benchmark for evaluating self-evolving agents in long-horizon, interdependent task streams. It covers daily office work, multi-turn dialogue, and AutoResearch-style workflows, with persistent workspaces and dependencies across tasks. The benchmark includes two complementary levels: \textbf{L1}, which evaluates the acquisition and revision of language-expressible knowledge, and \textbf{L2}, which assesses the development of task-level capabilities through execution and feedback. Its evaluation further distinguishes within-task recovery, persistent-state updates, and experience reuse in later tasks. We evaluate five agent frameworks across three backbone configurations under three persistence conditions, covering 19,635 scored task slots from selected evaluation cohorts. Results show that no framework consistently performs best across both levels, retries recover only a limited proportion of failed tasks, and persistent-state updates do not necessarily improve subsequent performance. Furthermore, the effects of evolution differ between knowledge- and capability-level tasks, suggesting that these two forms of evolution require different learning mechanisms. Performance gains also vary across domains and task streams, with improvements on some tasks not necessarily extending to others.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 EvoLink-Bench，用于评测长程且任务间相互依赖的任务流中的自进化 agent，覆盖办公事务、多轮对话与 AutoResearch 工作流，分 L1（语言可表达知识的获取与修正）和 L2（借助执行与反馈形成任务级能力）两层，并区分任务内恢复、持久状态更新与后续任务中的经验复用。
AI.relevance_reason: 其对持久工作区与跨任务状态复用的分层评测，以及「状态更新未必提升后续表现」的观察，可能为核查 LVR 中 latent 状态是否真被后续推理使用提供评价思路；但对象为纯文本 agent 场景，与视觉证据筛选的关联需自行判断。
